headline: Sets rules for how federal agencies work with religious and community groups that use federal money to provide social services.
what_it_does: This order updates an earlier order (Executive Order 13279) on federal partnerships with faith-based and neighborhood groups. It says groups getting federal social service funds may not turn away people based on religion. Openly religious activities must be kept separate from federally funded services and must be voluntary. People who object to a provider's religious character can ask for a different provider, and the order set up a working group of agencies to write guidance on these rules.

who_it_affects.group: Religious and community organizations that receive federal social service funds
who_it_affects.how: They must keep religious activities separate from funded services and serve people of any faith, while still keeping their religious identity.

who_it_affects.group: People who receive federally funded social services
who_it_affects.how: They cannot be turned away for their religion, do not have to take part in religious activities, and can ask for an alternative provider.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that fund social service programs
who_it_affects.how: They must follow these principles, tell people about their protections, and take part in shared guidance work.
